211183.overview: Magica is a single-screen platform game inspired by classics like 'Snow Bros' or 'Bubble Bobble' which was originally released by Juan J. Martinez for the Amstrad-CPC computers. The Amiga port is provided by Andy Noble. It is a nice mix of Snow Bros, Bubble Bobble and Tumblepop.

211184.overview: Max Knight is a platform game where the eponymous knight has to rescue his brother who has been taken away by a dragon. The game is made up of 36 single screen levels in five worlds and the objective in each is to collect all keys and other items and head for the exit. At the same time there are numerous enemies, animals and evil creatures, that have to be avoided by jumping over them. Any contact with an enemy leads to one out of five lives being lost but it is possible to refill them by collecting hearts. On some levels there are levers that need to be pulled to progress.

211185.overview:
Chances are that you have played a card memory game many times before... but not this way!
MeMO is a card memory game whose peculiarity is that it allows two players to play simultaneously - that is, they can flip cards at the same time and battle for the best score! Also, it does not drive players mad due to bad luck, as unlucky moves are ignored - and, well, to say it all, lucky moves aren't rewarded either.
With its neat graphics, which pay a little tribute to the Amiga and some of its games, and cool music, MeMO will take you for a pleasant trip down the memory (heh!) lane.

211186.overview:
Also published in the Amiga Format coverdisk 100b. Monty The Wolf, by Andy Sherratt, from 1992, A really excellent platformer written in AMOS. You play as Monty The Wolf, You control Monty throughout the Levels, in which your main aim is to collect all the diamonds to complete the level, while avoiding or killing the many animals which will try to kill you

There are various animals around who will try and stop you, such as Hedgehogs, Snails and Flying Birds, These can all be jumped over or avoided, But you can also kill them, as you happen to have a Green Ball, which you can throw at them to knock them out a few times, and a final throw will kill them and reveal item pickups which have various effects

211193.overview: Magiczna Ksiega is a platform game, developed by Midnight Computer Games and published by Mirage Interactive, which was released in Europe in 1994. Nice story, nice graphics and animation, lacking in action. Written in AMOS. Game scenario & coding by Pawe? Miko?ajczak. Graphics by Adam Karol and Pawe? Miko?ajczak. Music by Robert Chojnacki and Krzysztof Sobiera?ski.

211224.overview: Search the level. Pick up all items and make it to the door out before time runs out.

211225.overview: Collect mysteries, gain extra time...gain extra lives in this Boulder Dash like game.  Collect gems of four color types, blow up objects or use teleporters to get to blocked-off parts of the screen, and avoid baddies.

211230.overview: A challenging crosshairs shooter game from LK Avalon. Miasto Śmierci is a science fiction shooter. A mad scientist wants to take control over the world. As a secret agent the player is equipped with a combat robot called MOA. MOA is equipped with a scanner, five types of weapons and an early warning system. During the action unmanned aircraft supply ammunition. The goal is to penetrate enemy territory and gain the scientific research. The same task has been entrusted by two foreign countries to theirs agents: Russia sent Ivan Michalkov and from Germany, Hans Kahlert. The agent moves through the city map and encounter traps (like a mine field) or enemies. The duel with enemies takes place on a single first person perspective screen. Using one of five types of weapons the player must kill a designated number of terrorists to get back to the city map.

211232.overview: Miecze Valdgira II: Władca Gór is an action-adventure game. This time king Aldir must defeat Bloody Zenon, that uses Cyclops eye to terrorize the surrounding area. Aldir must wander the surrounding forest and underground labyrinth, collecting one-use items along the way and using them in the right places, mostly to open underground passages. Each location is inhabited by hostile creatures. Contact with the creatures for longer than two seconds means instant death. The best way to circumvent the enemy is jumping over or passing under them.

211233.overview: A new rescue-the-hostages game where you eliminate terrorists.

211234.overview: Based on the 1984 Spectrum graphic adventure THE WILD BUNCH from Firebird Software, MOBSTERS CITY has a gangster theme although Western elements such as the shootout remain. Search for the local villains and if necessary, take them out in this light-hearted and fun game.

211235.overview: Motorola Invaders 2 is a Space Invaders type game in which you are trying to save your computer from viruses. The viruses come swarming down randomly and they don't fire at you. When you shoot one virus, it falls, and if it hits you on the way down you'll lose one life. You'll also lose one life if a virus reaches the ground alive. There are eight levels in game and there is no score, you just need to shoot all aliens. In game music is sampled song from Metallica, Sad But True.

211236.overview: A puzzle game based on Sokoban levels. It has great music, smooth scrolling, supports passwords for each level and has a level editor. published in Amiga Fun (UK) no. 6, Apr 1991, Amiga Mania no. 3, Jun 1992  and in Amiga Fun Gold Edition (DE) no. 2, 1993. A collision of the space vessel Vega VII with an asteroid rips tertium containers filled with plasma away from its anchors. The plasma containers must be fastened down again with the help of  a droid, which you control! All containers must be pushed to an anchor. A control lamp on top of the container indicates when it is secure. The level finishes when all the containers are correctly secure. Do it in as few moves as possible.

211256.overview: A single screen, top down puzzler created by Holger Schemel for Artsoft. Mirror Magic is a basic puzzle game that works almost the same way as another popular game titled Deflector. In the game, the great magician Mc Duffin sends a beam of light and a number of men holding mirrors have to deflect the beam of light by changing the way they hold the mirror in their hands. You have to keep changing the mirror angles and the light beam path to do two things – destroy the unwanted objects and hit the beam of light on the exit door. As you hit the exit door, you are moved to the next level.

211257.overview:
Far, far away from planet earth in another galaxy there is a planet called "Terror" where the Wizard of Terror is up to his tricks. He built a mighty empire and created a new species of monsters never seen in the universe before. Those monsters, formed to an army of darkness, are unfeeling, unscrupulous and willing to kill for their master. With this army the mad wizard is about to extinguish all humanity.

Our four heroes discovered the subterranean headquarter of the Wizard of Terror and his evil army, before he could execute his crazy plan. Now it is your turn to defeat the army of darkness and the Wizard or Terror...

211258.overview:
MR BEANBAG! was originally planned for commercial release by Alten8/Retro-Soft in late 2005, but the publishing deal fell through after coder Amy Worthington (Tricky) secured a new job causing development to run overtime. The final release is now expected to be freeware and should appear in 2011/12, although a boxed copy is being considered for sale direct from the developers if there is enough interest expressed by Amigans. [Source: Interview with Amy Worthington (Jan 2012), Chris Clarke/Amigapd.com] 
 
MR BEANBAG! is a SONIC THE HEDGEHOG clone that was originally coded for the A500 in AMOS by Amy Worthington (Tricky) back in the Amiga heyday. In early 2005 she rediscovered her passion for Amiga coding and began porting the game in AMOS to AGA machines, but decided to optimise the code by converting it into 100% ASM.

211376.overview:
Madhouse: Indian Spirit is a graphic adventure for the Amiga created with AMOS. Unusually for an adventure of this type, the player uses joystick controls instead of the mouse, and only left/right movement is used. You interact with things you are standing next to (or in front of) with the fire button. There is no inventory management or conversation trees, and instead of a save-game system, each chapter has its own password.

The hero of Madhouse is Greg Kapschnitz, janitor of the Valverdance mental institution. He discovers that there is a plan to tear down the building to make way for a highway, and is determined to help save the facility.

211377.overview: A fun platforming game that came with a level editor. It features 5 levels of difficulty as you make your way around the levels gathering prizes and trophies and avoiding traps and jumping over skull and crossbones to get to the exit keyholes.

211541.overview: A mouse themed beat-em-up from our Australian friends at ECP.

211553.overview: You play as Max Knight and must traverse through 36 levels challenging levels in 5 worlds, collecting items, avoiding enemies and finally free your brother from the evil dragon! Originally released as a demo, but full version is now out.

211648.overview: Match Patch was released on CU Amiga (Dec 1991), Amiga Action 62 (Oct 1994), The One Amiga 47 (Aug 1992). A fun but hard platform game. You drop down the holes to change your weapon, but the enemies will also change when they drop down the holes. Your goal is to clear the screen of enemies before time runs out. There are five enemy types, and each can only be killed by bullets of its own type. (Fire beats fire, ice beats ice… this is opposite to modern game design thinking, perhaps because this was 1990 and Pokémon wasn’t invented yet.)

211674.overview: The game resembles "Harlequin" for Amiga, and features multiple different levels and characters for you to control.

211801.overview: Miroslaw Kontra Slawomir Czyli Walka o Tron is an Action game, developed by Domain Software and published by EXE, which was released in Europe (Poland) in 1995. Tron is an arcade side-scrolling fantasy beat-'em-up, a simplified clone of Golden Axe. As one of twin brothers the player must cross several lands defeating numerous legions of enemies to meet his relative in the final battle for the throne. Each level is divided into three stages. After the second stage an energy carrier appears, allowing to improve the health condition. The hero may derive three strokes - standard, in a kneeling position and aerial. Encountered enemies are divided into three groups: flying, walking and jumping, each with only one kind of attack. Some of defeated enemies leave a grey shield, which gives a temporary immortality. The game allows to choose one of two available background sets.

211880.overview: A military themed vertically scrolling shooter and sequel to Raid, created by Fez Software using the Shoot-'Em-Up-Construction Kit (SEUCK). It was described by the team as a SWIV tribute. This version is a little less difficult than the original, but the graphics are slightly improved. Tough, addictive and a bargain.

211951.overview: An unofficial amiga port created by Kevin Gallagher. The player's six cities are being attacked by an endless hail of ballistic missiles, some of which split like multiple independently targetable reentry vehicles. New weapons are introduced in later levels: smart bombs that can evade a less-than-perfectly targeted missile, and bomber planes and satellites that fly across the screen launching missiles of their own. As a regional commander of three anti-missile batteries, the player must defend six cities in their zone from being destroyed.

212012.overview:
A flip-screen platform/adventure game with influences from Dizzy and old 8-bit platformers.  It features a 29-screen level, with a number of puzzles to solve and characters to converse with, as Maxwell the Mouse attempts to retrieve an Amiga game mysteriously taken from his home. Maxwell the cool blue mouse (who insists on wearing sunglasses and a backpack) had just woken up after a very pleasant night's sleep. He was excited because just yesterday, he had gone and bought a fabulous new Amiga game. He had given the game pride of place in his special disk box ready to be played as soon as he got up that morning.

But disaster had struck. The disk wasn't there. The box was empty. It hadn't been left in his Amiga's disk drive. In fact, it was nowhere to be seen. "Oh, botheration! My floppy diskette appears to have gone missing. This is a most unfortunate turn of events", is something Maxwell didn't quite say but as it's before the watershed... well, that was the gist of it.

There's only one real explanation - someone must have got in, somehow, and stolen it. But how? Who? Why? In the absence of anything worthwhile to do, Maxwell decides to go on a little adventure to try and retrieve his game. After all, it's a small village, and there are one or two shady characters lurking about. Not everyone likes Maxwell and indeed, not everyone likes the Amiga...

212072.overview: Here you have Meteor Defender, an arcade classic, made with Amos Professional. The mission is to prevent the meteors destroying the city, which is protected by a force field.

212150.overview: Game written in AMOS. Coding, graphics & music/sound FX by Ola Zandelin. Additional level design by Daniel Zandelin.  Game includes a built-in construction kit and instructions. Game is available on 17-Bit PD disk #3305, PD-Soft disk #4248 and Assassins CD#2. Inspired by Tony Crowther's BOMBUZAL, the very first version of MARBLES developed was called BB BALL and was never officially released. A few years later, the graphics were updated, a construction kit included and the name was changed to MARBLES when coder Ola Zandelin finally released his first complete version of the game in 1991 to the eager Amiga masses. When asked what inspired the game, Zandelin had this to say:

212210.overview:
Thomas Agermose Jensen brings Nintendo's famous character Mario (and Luigi) to the Amiga in this unoffical conversion of the C64 Mario Bros game. Interestingly, Ocean released a Mario Bros game on the C64 but there was also another unreleased conversion by Atarisoft. The gameplay is classic Mario Bros with the two plumbers clearing out sewers by headbutting platforms from below to knock over various creatures or by using the limited use POW button which overturns all enemies on the screen at the same time.

The developer Thomas found the disk for Mario Bros when working through his old floppy collection. It would never have been released commercially due to issues of copyright but could have been a freeware game if released in 1993.

212211.overview:
This Arkanoid Pong\Breakout style game is the equel to Megaball and precursor to Megaball v3. A bat and ball block breaker game, in which you have a bat at the bottom of the screen which you can only move left and right using the mouse, and shoot a Ball upwwards into blocks which break, some take a few hits to break, while others may even appear on the play area when the ball hits an invisible block

You will also need to follow the Ball with your Bat and stop it from exiting the bottom of the screen by hitting it back up into the Blocks

If you lose the Ball down below, this will cost you a Life, in this case, it will give you a new bat at the bottom of the screen, allowing you to continue play, until all your Bats are exhausted, at which point its Game Over, Game Over Maaaan!

212260.overview: Graphics ripped straight out of Yoshi's Island and what was added looks amateurish at best. The player sprites have too few frames of animation. Despite the omnipresence of ladders in the levels, there is no animation for ladder climbing, so Blip and Blop awkwardly "wiggle" up and down when they use them. On the plus side, the background music is quite good and the game is at least playable, brief as it is. I guess there was a bit of a novelty factor in seeing Nintendo and Studio Peyo characters brutally exploded and dismembered. Too me, it looks childish. In 2004, an updated and expanded version of Blip & Blop was released for Windows.

212439.overview: Written in Blitz Basic 2. Coding & graphics by Jim Marshall. Music by Stuart Radforth. A cute platformer where you need to avoid the tops, ducks and toys to go over every diamond. Once all the diamonds have been touched you will moved to the next level. Items can help you solve the levels.

212496.overview: An unreleased platform shooter from Livewires/Electric Software that was set for release in 1989, coded by Adrian Robert Cummings.

212499.overview: The unregistered Shareware version of Marathon includes only the two-player option. It's quite fun. You and an opponent chase each other through a small residential district. The gameplay is similar to Carnage, Brutal Homicide or Extreme Violence. One difference in Marathon is the ability to enter and drive cars.

212735.overview:
MazezaM is a puzzle game, where the player has to pass through the levels by sliding the walls to left and right, opening corridors between. The rules seem simple, but the game gets harder and harder as the stages go on further. Sometime, the reach to the end seem unsolvable, but there is always a solution at the beginning. If a level is rendered by the player unsolvable, there is a possibility for a replay in the room from the initial position, but this is at the cost of a life. After all the lives are used, the game is over and have to be started again from the first level. If the level room is passed, the player is rewarded with extra life, which comes handy in the next levels. 
 
The newest Amiga version have fourty-two levels, talking intro and nice outro sequence. Some of the rooms are small and very easy to overcome, but some of them are wide and a real headache to pass. Game created by Ventzislav Tzvetkov aka drHirudo.

212752.overview: Tetris with pastels and tomatoes, blocking cubes and other fun surprises. As usual, when the pieces reach the top your game is over. Created by Marco Aricati and released as freeware in 1993.

212753.overview: A 200 level puzzler from 1993, the freeware game by Testaware. The game was released as part of the Assassins CD 02. A strategic game where you must turn stone numbers by clicking it to a given order. If one is selected all bordering stones will change it’s number too. More about 200 random generated levels. Game concept based on Logo by Starbyte.

212758.overview:
This is Mother Lode by Joe Rumsey (Night Owl Software), yet another good Lode Runner clone of sorts, The basic principle here is exactly the same as the other Lode Runner games

You start off flashing, in this mode the game is in effect “Paused” so it gives you time to study the level, and plan your route to collect all the Gold Bars, and then finally head for freedom at the top of the level

You have to collect the Gold Bars while avoiding the Red Men who will come after you, although the AI is a little strange at times and you will find them getting confused quite easily, you can easily avoid the Red Men by digging a hole, and standing back so that they will fall into the hole, thereby allowing you to walk over their heads and carry on the platform, However they only stay in the hole for a short time, before they leap back out and then proceed to hunt you down (unless the hole fills in, in that case, it will kill them and they will respawn at the top of the screen, flashing for a few seconds, before again coming after you)

You can climb the ladders and swing off the ropes (shown as lines on the screen) and even fall off the rope half-way so collect any Gold Bars which maybe suspended in mid-air, this is also a quick way to escape the Red Men, as you can go across the rope, let go, although as you do, any Men following you will also let go, and fall down, so you need to vacate the area quickly before they land nearby and start hunting you down again

To clear a level, you must collect all the Gold Bars, then proceed to the very top of the screen, at which point you will clear the level and the next one will show, then you will start flashing so you can have a good look at the level before moving, which will then start the game again

213521.overview:
Maria Renard's Revenge is an Amiga Castlevania fan game developed by Domkid using the Scorpion Engine.

You play as Maria Renard,  she is a young vampire huntress, daughter of distant kinship with the House of Belmont, who has to traverse through dangerous landscapes and fight many monsters, while defending herself with the use of a bird that protects her from harm...

213589.overview:
MasterType is an educational game that teaches the player how to type with the keyboard. In the game the MasterType is a powerful wizard who is helping the player defending his command ship by using his laser like force. The command ship is stationed in the center of the screen and from each corner of the screen missiles are launched toward the ship. In each corner of the screen there is a word and by successfully typing in these words the wizard uses his force to zap the missiles. The command ship has four areas and when an area has been hit by a missile it's shield will be destroyed. If the same area is hit a second time the whole ship will explode and the game will be over.

The game consists of 17 or 18 lessons depending on version and is chosen before the game begins. The first lesson deals with the home row keys (a to ;) and the player only has to enter single letters. As the difficulty increases with each lesson longer and more complex phrases needs to be typed in. Once a lesson is completed the player gets a summary showing how well he has done and whether further practice is needed. Some options exist to alter the game after the player's needs. A beginner mode can be turned on and it's also possible to set a speed goal (number of words per minute). In addition to the lessons included, it is also possible for the player to create his own lessons.

213606.overview:
An educational game featuring 6 mini-games that focus on memory, color and shape recognition.
Programmed in AmigaBasic.

213607.overview: MathTalk is a mathematical based educational game that is suitable for children aged 5-15.

214074.overview:
Magician's Dungeon is a full graphics and text adventure. Most every room has a full screen graphic, taking advantage of the Amiga's great graphics, color and cycling ability. You control your characters action through keyboard, menus or mouse. Type the commands you want and follow your instincts and wit.
Can you save the land? If you dare?

214075.overview: Professor Matt A. Matics of MATHTALK fame is back again! This time he's ready to help you master Fractions, Decimals and Percents. You enter your own problems to check your homework. The professor has also cooked up some exciting games that challenge you to solve all types of problems, particularly those that show the inter-relationship between Fractions, Decimals and Percents. Get ready for new confidence in math class as you check your work in the Problem Factory, meet the Team Challenge, out-wager the professor in Fraction Shuffle and get the highest score in the Fun House.

214078.overview: Mindbreaker is a Breakout clone, developed by Digital Artwork and published by Softgang, which was released in Europe in 1987.

214178.overview: What is this? How could you be driving your Datsun, and suddenly you are somewhere else? Is it the future or the past? Is it nowhere? Maybe it is a nightmare. All you have is a spikey ball on a chain. A MACE, that's it. That's what they used to call it. It mast be the past, but something tells you it's not. But you have no time to think, only to fight. No time to work out if this is only a dream. If these creatures kill you , you may wake up. And then again you might not....

214179.overview: Macho Killers is a simple cross-hairs shooting game: From time to time there appear bad guys on the screen. You must try to shoot faster than them. If you play well you can enter your name on the high score table.

214180.overview:
This quite simple little game is called Mad Bomber created by David Papworth in 1991

You are a set of Black Tyres at the bottom of the screen, and your job is to catch all the Bombs the Mad Bomber drops, if you miss even one of them, You lose a life and have to carry on until Game Over

The Mad Bomber drops them from side-to-side, and changes direction mid-stream, so you have to be very quick to be able to keep up, ideally if you use the Mouse instead of the Joystick, You move a lot quicker and can catch many more

As you start off, the Bombs are dropped quite slowly, but as the levels increase the Bombs get faster and the Mad Bomber moves back and forth more quickly, it will take a lot of skill to keep up with him on later levels

There is no music here, just the sounds of Bombs dropping and being captured by the Tyres, and at the top, you have your Lives displayed on the left, Game information pops up in the top-middle, and finally you have your Score top-right, There is no High Score Table here, it simply shows your previous score on the title screen when Game Over occurs

214181.overview: It is called Mad Crash Racing but this isn't about racing for first, it is about avoid an accident with your beautiful red sport car. Do not drive the wrong way on the road. Press Space button to change the lane. Press Esc to quit game. The game will save the high-scores to the disk if it is not write protected. Warning! Be patient. Do not kill your good old Amiga while playing this game. Mad Crash Racing is the first game developed by József Trencsényi. In 1999, he founded the independent game developer company Artex Studios.

214182.overview: Gather up the goodies and make your way to the exit. You only have a certain number of bombs, so use them wisely. Careful of the acid, the nasties and all the hazards of this crazy mayhem factory. Well-made game in which a worker has to find his way out of the different halls (levels) of a factory. Various tools are available, such as keys, diamonds, bombs, etc. With many levels (60) and a very comfortable, mouse-controlled editor for your own game scenes. With two-player mode and German instructions.

214185.overview: A one on one fighting game from EK Man created in 1994 and released to the public domain.

214197.overview: Our task is to get the ball to the exit by jumping on the different platforms. The game was created using the WinUAE emulator and works well on it. Remember that some platforms are safe and others are full of danger, enemies. Find the keys to open the locks. Pull the switch, climb the ladder, get more energy and use the teleporter, avoid the spikes and make your way to the exit.

214198.overview: A collection of solitaire games from PRZsoft, which is Frank Przybylski  and  Stefan Przybylsk. Magic Cards is a selection of 19 fascinating patiences, whose difficulty vary from easy to pretty hard. You can choose between the English and the German version.

214199.overview:
Magic Coins is a puzzle board game for up to two human or computer players. The aim requires taking over as many opponents coins as possible. Coins may be moved in two ways, by multiplication (jump on the adjacent field) or simple changing position (jump two squares from the current spot). Placing the coin next to opponent's coins causes acquisition. The game continues until the inability to make a move or acquiring of all coins on the board.

The game features the level editor, allowing the change the number of start up coins (2 to 6) and background type.

214201.overview: Another puzzler from Harald Müller (Mueller) released by multiple companies in 1995. Lay out the arrows and instructions given in front of the ball to allow it to hit all the coins and make it to the black exit square. You have four balls to do all the work and there is a counter next to each telling you how many instructions you get to lay out to reach your goal. Good luck

214202.overview: A simply styles version of shanghai mahjong created by Franz Janisch and released in the year 2000.

214203.overview: A nice version of mahjong for 1 or 2 players, from Cynet\Rebl with music by Stargate\Ulysses, released in 1996. In game this is also known as "dragon tiles", a western variant on the Asian game. Contains multiple different game types and tiles.

214204.overview: A Snake clone published on the cover disk of Amiga Action 38 (Nov 1992).

214205.overview: Here you must turn patterns with different colored balls on it to create single color ones. It’s not a well gameplay but it will get harder as much as patterns to solve. Very simple graphics I think.

214206.overview: An Amigan version of the board game Sorry!, created by Niels Böhm and released as public domain in 1999. The game allow up to 4 to play.

214207.overview: An adult puzzle game by Fabrizio Bazzo and released in 1994 where completing the board gives you an adult themed manga picture. It starts off pretty standard and then REALLY ramps things up.

214208.overview: Embrace the adrenaline of Mangled Fenders: Armored Combat Edition, a game where six human or controlled tanks duel in close quarters in smash em up derby would be if they allowed munitions. Collect your cash and victory points

214210.overview: There were at least two variants of Manic Miner for the Commodore Amiga, the Mayhem Miner variant is a PD Freeware version for one player and is more compatible with different Amiga configurations. Very tough to spot any differences between this game and commercial versions.

214211.overview: Part of the Chess Replacement Project. Manipulation, by Justin Kolb, is a complex strategy game in the long line of games of this type, updates and replacements for Chess that might take us in different directions and open up new ideas and complexities. Manipulation is designed ofr 2 players sitting at the same computer and sharing the mouse. Gold player starts at the top of the 8x8 playing board and Silver is content to start at the bottom. Each side starts out with 16 pieces total, there are 8 different types of pieces, 2 of each type. The game revolves around one type of piece which is called the Blank. All pieces look like coins with different faces to differentiate them. The Blank is just that. When you run out of Blank pieces, the game is over. Activate the piece you want to move and move it by clicking where you want to go.

214213.overview: Marble Rescue is a puzzle race against time, developed and published by Amigo!, which was released in Europe in 1994. The ball will travel forward and will tend towards right turns as it hits flat walls, but will follow the wall if it hits a corner. You have a limited amount of directionals allowed: Up, down, left and right markers that will tell the ball to follow them. Use them to avoid the bombs and to get all the dots and make it to the exit spot!

214214.overview: Push the balls into the brown spaces in the least moves possible. They start you off easy and it gets a bit harder every level. Make sure you don't cut off your path to victory.  You can only push one ball at a time, no more than one.

214215.overview: The whole screen is a giant slider (Fifteen) puzzle, but this one is 11x10. You must QUICKLY slide things around to allow you to move the ball from the starting position to the end piece. The ball will happily stay for a short while in the starting position, so get some places joined together to allow it to move before letting it out of the first section. Game is very challenging and came with a level editor.

214216.overview: A Pang clone written by Luca Carminati and released in 1997. Use the joystick to guide Marietto, filling the bricks one at a time. Press fire to kick enemies and P to pause. You gain a new life every 10k points. If you pick up all the coins you get 500 points. Every third coin taken will generate a power-pill, swallow it and become temporarily invulnerable to everything except bombs, nigh invulnerable! Bombs kill you, however they also kill every alien on the screen. Kick the daggers to avoid them or run over while nigh invulnerable. Bumping rocks can only happen when nigh invulnerable, otherwise they will crush you. Fling the bricks against the flying aliens, you may also be able to kick them if you are very skilled and somewhat bendy. When the going gets tough, the aliens will start shooting, so be ready for it when it happens! Bouncing aliens can be killed similarly. Drills cannot be kicked, but use nigh invulnerability against them.

214217.overview: Martial Morphers was released by F1 Licenceware on disk F1-104. Game written in AMOS Professional. Coding by Lee Bamber, it is an IK+ clone, it is also an International Karate + clone, where you control your two fighters simultaneously as a single fighting force. Defeat your enemy, with your ability to control two separate fights at the same time. Both fighters respond to every controller command, creating and easy system that is quickly picked up. The first to achieve 4 knock-out strikes wins a bout. Each match can have 3, 5 or 7 bouts against the computer or an additional human player. Above all, it's a beat'em up like no other, based on accuracy, speed, maneuverability and cunning skill. You will in time, become one with the metal fighters.

214218.overview: A two-player fighting game created by Black Paladins and released in 1992.

214219.overview:
Masa Krytyczna is a puzzle game for two players. The aim of the game is to eliminate all the chips of the opponent. The tiles on the gameplay board have from two up to four slots. Each tile may adopt only one color chips. After filling all the slots explosive reaction occurs and the chips are scattered to adjacent tiles. The post explosion spreading may result in filling the adjacent tiles, starting a chain reaction - the reaction continues until stepping on an unfilled tile. If the opponents adjacent plate has only one free slot explosion spread causes acquisition of the tile. 
 
Game was added as a free bonus game in the 1992 release of Skarabeusz.

214220.overview: A public domain golf game from D. Cameron and released in 1992.

214221.overview: A Worms style head to head shooter for one or two players.

214222.overview: Masquerade is an Amiga puzzle game from Cynet released in 1994. It's a puzzle game featuring 40 levels. Gather all the gems and make it back to the exit, but with explosions to avoid and portcullis to avoid, and all this in only a certain number of moves. Some exits don't show until you've hit the flag to make it appear.

214223.overview: Master Mind, by Mark Bishop is a simple clone of the classic board game with the same name. A five color code sequence is assumed that you must guess. You have 12 tries to figure it out by trying different color combinations. A number at the top shows the number you have of the right color, the pins at the bottom show the ones you have in the right sequence. Now crack the combination!

214224.overview: Match the pictures in this memory game created by Vision X and released in 1994.

214225.overview: It's all a numbers game in this two-player only puzzler from Alon Fliess and Alon Ginosar. Player 1 plays numbers in the horizontal, player two plays numbers in the vertical. The option is to collect higher numbers than the other player. The game will be over when all the numbers in the row or column has finished. The winner will be the one who has more points. Seems way too simple, but it is a beast to play.

214226.overview: Something very much like Arkanoid that contains a built in editor program to make your own levels. This version by Stefano Maria Regattin was released in 2002 but has had many updates and improvements.

214227.overview:
A three player card game created by Harald Müller (Mueller) and published in Gamer's Delight, Gamer's Delight 2 and in Schatztruhe #1209. Mau-Mau is a member of the larger Crazy Eights or shedding family, to which the proprietary card game Uno belongs. However Mau-Mau is played with standard French or German-suited playing cards. The game is typically played with a 32-card pack, either a French-suited pack from which the Twos, Threes, Fours, Fives and Sixes have been removed or, especially in Europe, with a 32-card German pack. For more than 5 players, 2 packs of cards may be used.

The aim is to be first to get rid of all of one's cards. Most of the time, the winner will have to say something at this point, usually "Mau". If they fail to say this, they do not win and instead must take penalty cards. If a player's last card is a Jack, they must reply differently, usually saying "Mau Mau".

214228.overview: Avoid the nasties like the crapmonster, the burning sun and the weedmonster and gather all the goodies like flowers, game disks and hearts. There are 8 worlds to explore and a password save function. Game by Gavilian Ruiz aka Hawk aka focataku of the group Future Brain. This is a sequel to May & Yam 1, which was only for two players.

214229.overview: Mayhem is an arena game by Mark Green for 2 to 4 players all at the same time. It is best played with 3 or 4 players. You can adjust dead time, shots to kill, no of shots, moving exits and transporters as well as choosing one of nine mazes.

214230.overview: You collect keys in mazes while avoiding enemies with predictable movement patterns. A PD game created by Frederic Cordier aka FreddiX in 1993.

214231.overview: A collect'em up maze game created B. L. Gaunt and released in 1994. Published in F1 Licenceware CD-Rom Volume One F1-001 To F1-100. Maze Madness takes the formula aesthetics from Rally-X and puts them into a maze from Pac-Man.

214232.overview: A Pac-Man clone by Steve Eaborn who is the sole employee of Mr. E Software, it was created in AMOS and has 16 levels.

214233.overview: A labyrinth solving game for two players from Lee Atkins released in 1997. You can choose the complexity of the mazes you compete to solve.

214234.overview: A multiplayer game loosely based on an ancient networkable game from the1970's. From one to eight players move droids around a maze armed with a single missile shooter and their wits. This is a game with no beginning and no end. It is a continuous battle for supremacy.  This game supports linking two or more computers to play if desired. From one to 4 on each computer. The computer can also control unused droids, with an adjustable reaction time. Two mazes are selected and played simultaneously and changes can happen to the maze on the fly. There are 16 mazes to choose from and a converter is included to allow you to design your own. Each player has a Haven in which special abilities can be purchased with cash gained from shooting other players. No shooting happens in Haven.

214239.overview: Did you enjoy Megaball 2.1 and 3.0, how about Megaball 4.0 for AGA? Well how about the game that started it all for the Mackey brothers, the Ball before it was Mega! This Arkanoid-style Block Breaker Game lets you play the original incarnation.

214240.overview: A clone of Tetris for 1 or 2 players created by Dominic Ramsey in Amos and released to PD in 1993. This game was included in the Assassins ASI-GAMES-VOL 155 compilation.

214241.overview: If you get only one Tetris game for the Amiga, make sure this is the one. Well written with great performance and visuals, very nice music. This one also has blocks not seen in other versions. Includes a really well done two player mode. Part of the Active Software Ground Zero game collection. The is the sequel to the original MegaBlock game.

214242.overview: Here's a Boulderdash/Emerald Mines clone with some differences: the boulders and diamonds don't fall diagonally, and although the colours stay the same, the background graphics change from level to level. Things like tree roots, toxic waste containers, and Pupsi cans are scattered throughout. Game created by Martin Thron and Michael Gerhards and released in 1995.  The game consists of 40 stages, and every 4 we get the code so you can continue it later.

214243.overview: A version of Megaman for the Amiga created by Reentier and made with Backbone, released in 2014. Mega Man is a side-scrolling platform game. It is up to the blue robot Megaman to stop the baddies by jumping and shooting his way past an army of robots.

214244.overview:
Megasquad is a two-player combat-style game with two different modes of gameplay:  Tag and Duel.  Both game modes are played on boards consisting of walls and gates, and there are many boards to choose from.  You may either choose a board each time you play, or you can have the computer pick a random board.

Control:  The control is based on rotation and thrust.  Each player controls a ship, and the ship is rotated left and right with the joystick.  Thrust can
be applied by pressing up on the joystick.  In duel mode, the fire button fires a shot.  Player 1 uses joystick #1 (the free joystick port) and player
2 uses joystick #0 (the mouse port).

The object of tag is to accumulate a certain amount of points before your opponent does.  The player who is not 'IT' accumulates two points per
second.  The player who is 'IT' must try to tag the opponent.  When the player who is 'IT' tags the opponent, the opponent becomes 'IT'.  There is a three-second getaway time, and during this time no points are accumulated. At the beginning of a Tag game there is a scramble to determine which
player starts out as 'IT'.  Both players are placed at an equal distance from a red line, and the last player to cross the line starts out the tag match as
'IT'.  There are six different scramble boards, and you can select which one is used, or you can have the computer select a random one each game.  This is done from the option screen.

Duel:   The object of the duel game is to shoot your opponent and avoid getting shot.  You accumulate one point each time you kill your opponent, and your opponent accumulates a point when he kills you.  The first player to get a certain number of points wins the game.  There is a three-second invincibility which takes effect at the beginning of the game and whenever a player dies and reappears.

214245.overview: Released by Dragon at the Grace group at The Party 1991, this is another Snake\Worm\Tronic Jetbike game for two players, with no computer players supported.

214246.overview: A Tron inspired Snake\Worm game for up to 7 humans and a total of 10 other players! IN it you steer a rasterbike and have to kill the other players by jamming them and forcing them into a wall. To make this easier, you and your opponents have access to three weapons from an arsenal of nine. Like in real life, nothing is free. Although the weapon's ammunition is unlimited, all of them cost a certain amount of money. You earn money by simply staying alive or by killing another player. If you have exterminated all opponents you will enter the next round with now more than 1000 credits in your pockets and 2 bonus points. Use those points to fund your next set up weapons!

214247.overview: Megaworm which was written by Kirk D’Souza in Devpac 3, is a take on a classic Worm game, in which you have to pick up dots to progress through the game's 50 levels. The Special Powerups are as follows: Light Green increases you speed for 10 seconds, Dark Green decreases speed, Purple doubles the length of your worm, Pink shortens your worm, Red gives you a new life, Orange gives you more points for moving, Blue turns all the worms Blue, so on a level with lots of barriers, this would make it more difficult for example, Light Blue gives Invunerability for 10 seconds, Yellow reverses the controls of the opposite player (so if computer gets this one, expect lots of fun heh), and Grey switches off the lights, so you can only see a small part of the screen around your snake for 20 seconds!

214248.overview: A memory game by Walter Claude et Beh Claude and released in 1998. Zero to two people can play. You are about to see your ability to memorize the location of weird black shapes skyrocket!

214249.overview: A board game version of the Memory game created in 24 hours that manages to be more interesting than the majority of games in this genre. Great pictures make for memorable items to harken back to. This one was created by Dawnbringer and released in 2000.

214250.overview: This may look like a PD game, but it was a commercial product and reviewed by Germany's most famous Amiga games magazine in 1993. The game was sold in German speaking countries only - Germany, Austria and Switzerland. It was something like Trivial Pursuit where you roll a die to move around the board answering questions in different categories to move to the game end.

214251.overview:
This is an unofficial port of Jeff Minter's Commodore VIC-20 and ZX Spectrum classic of the same name.

The Metallamas and Zzyaxians are at war with each other with the Zzyaxians attempting to overtake the Metallama's galaxy. The Zzyaxians have set their sights on taking over a small outpost called OP/37 on the rim of the galaxy to launch their attack. Problem is there are just three Metallamas and with no help nearby it is up to them to thwart the attack taking it in turns to defend the outpost. The Zzyaxians have sent Cyborg Arachnid Mutants who will use their threads to slide down into the outpost and destroy the Llamas.

You play as the Llama who can fire a bolt at a 45 degree angle upwards. You must try to hit each Mutant directly, if you hit their thread then they will drop down to the floor, turn into a Weeviloid and scurry towards the Llama. If you don't hit a Mutant or it's thread then they will drop to the floor at a certain point and once again scurry towards you as a Weeviloid. Each bolt fired can bounce of the ceiling and walls though so if you fail to hit the Mutant sliding down you can still kill the Weeviloid. One touch from a Weeviloid though and you lose one of your three Llama's. There are 32 levels to complete and you must kill 18 Mutants/Weeviloids a level to move on to the next.

Metagalactic Llamas: Battle at the Edge of Time is played on one screen with a side view. The game is a 1 or 2 player game where each player takes it in turn after a life is lost. You have the option to start on any level but the higher the level the more Mutants that slide down. As well as the main playing area you can see your score, lives and quota. You use a joystick to play.

214252.overview: A frenetic single-player, crosshairs shooter created by Robert Glavas and released in 1993.

214254.overview: Meteors is an Asteroids style shooter game from Harald Müller (Mueller), developed and published by Intersoft, which was released in Europe in 1994. It was republished in Gamers' Delight 2.

214255.overview: In this 1994 shareware game by Chris Glasspool, you must navigate through 10 levels of caverns. Collect all the crystals and fly off the top of the screen to complete a level. Complete the game by activating the terraforming device on level 10.

214256.overview: A vehicle simulator/shooter game for two players. The game feels like a two player version of Battlezone for the Amga and was written by Dirk Ketturkat, released in 1994 and later re-released in the Assassins Disk 174.

214257.overview: In METRO, you play the role of a city planner. Using limited funds, you must construct a mass-transit subway system capable of meeting the needs of your city. Build wisely and your system will be a success, but poor planning will lead to disaster and financial ruin. Shareware, binary only, source available from author. Author: Mark A. Thomas and David P. Townsend.

214258.overview: A public domain worm\snake collect'em up created by Phoenix Group and released in 1989. Snarf up the goodies, avoid the bugs and make your way to the exit. Bon apètit! A kind of 'Snake Byte'. Here, pills and various extras have to be collected under time pressure. The more you eat, the longer the snake's tail becomes. If you touch yourself or the walls of the labyrinth, you lose a life.

214259.overview: Mighty Mind is a reworking of the puzzler board game where you crack the 4 color code like Mastermind. White and black pegs tell you how many of the right color you have and how many are in the right location. If you can crack the code in 6 tries you have a mighty mind, indeed!

214260.overview: Based on 1988 Winchell Chung/ISM Apple IIGS release, MIGHTY MARVEL VS THE FORCES OF E.V.I.L., in it the player chooses a superhero and their opponent. The player has a number of superhero skills including: running, leaping, swimming, punching, lifting, and throwing. Each character has their own unique skills as well. There are 4 different scenarios, and 5 possible heroes. The player can explore the bank, the city, underground tunnels, and maze. Game contains a manual addendum on disk 1 (see 'Readme.MightyNerd' text file), as well as a standalone superhero character editor.

214261.overview: A version of the board game Mille Bornes for two players, created by John Scheib and John Toebes with fun sound effects and the Allelula Chorus when you beat the entire game.

214262.overview:
This card game derived from "Patience" is played with three card sets (96 cards in total). The upper and left edge is for the 12 aces, on which you have to stack cards in sequence of their numbers, which must exactly match in suit, too. If all cards have correctly been stacked on the aces, i. e. all the uppermost cards show a King, the game is won. The row of eight cards on the bottom edge is meant for interim placement of cards, i. e. if you are unable to find a matching card for any of the 12 decks. Here you have to lay the cards in the opposite sequence (King - 7), in which suits must be inverse, too. (e. g. if you have a King of Hearts, you can only lay a Queen of Clubs or a Queen of Spades.

Trivia:
The quotation shown on the end screen is an excerpt of the episode "Die Geschichte vom fliegenden Robert" (The Story of Flying Robert) from the 1845 children's book "Der Struwwelpeter" (Slovenly Peter) by Heinrich Hoffmann (1809-1894).

214263.overview:
Minerunner is a Lode Runner clone for up to four players. You (and friends) run around with a very small man on platforms and climb ladders collecting gold crates, while being hunted by equally small men. Defeat the enemies by digging holes in the platforms for them to fall into.

The game supports four simultaneous players using a four-player adapter, supports two-button joypads (so that you can dig both behind and in front of you) and is multitasking-friendly.

214265.overview: Quite a different from the original rules of Minesweeper. Select as much as possible minefree fields and got points for it. Two player mode, a good playing computer opponent, replay option save and load game functions and more.

214267.overview: On a planet XTROM, which is very far from the earth, are many minteral-mines. In 2008 a tremble damaged many mines and malicious aliens took up residence in the caves created by the earthquakes. You are a MineTrasher who must clear aliens and boulders from the mines while collecting the diamonds there. The caves are too small for more than a single-person vehicle, you must go in alone with your flamer, collect items and flame the monsters and boulders until your ship becomes green. Then reach the next beamstation and prepare for the next cave.

214268.overview: In Mink Gold, you collect golden balls in a maze while avoiding ghosts. You don't need to collect all golden balls, just enough to make a green key in the maze magically turn into a red key. You have to pick up this red key and exit via the door before the timer on the right side of the screen (lifted from North & South) runs out. Because you get only one life, beating all 16 levels is difficult.

214269.overview: A missile defense game written in 100% assembler with source available. The game was created by Glen Merriman and created in Summer-Fall 1986 and released to the public domain.

214270.overview:
An Amiga version of Missile command, a game by John Enright (credited as Max Bithead) that was released in 1990 and updated in 1991. Missile Command is a freeware remake of the classic arcade game.

As the commander of a missile base, it is your responsibility to defend cities from an attack. Missiles and other weapons descend from the top of the screen and to protect the cities your missiles must detonate in their flight path so that they get caught in the blast radius and destroyed. If anything gets through, one of your cities could be destroyed, when all the missiles are dealt with another wave begins, when all of the cities are gone, the game is over.

214275.overview:
Mission: Con-Bat is a vehicle simulation game, developed and published by Questrek, which was released in 1988. Even though the treaty was signed, there's no guarantee that missiles will not continue to be built and installed. For this reason, night reconnaissance missions will be lfown, in order to photograph possible illegal missile installations on designated island targets. Neither side wants to be found in non-compliance, therefore, these missions could prove to be very hazardous. Due to the high risk involved, all flights will be manned by volunteers. You'll have no offensive weaponry on board your aircraft. Instead, you'll be equipped with the finest state-of-the-art decoys, designed to draw enemy fire away from you. Radar jamming capabilities will offer some protection while precision mouse control provides excellent response time and maneuverability.  
 
A carrier will be standing by to receive you on completion of your missions. A refueler will also be scheduled to rendezvous with you at designated times. Your mission is to photograph enemy islands and land safely back on the carrier.

214276.overview: A horizontal shooter with soldier shown from an overhead view like Commando. Shoot and grenade your way through the enemy fortifications. It appears to have been created with the Shoot'em Up Construction set. This game was often bundled with PT45, for a land and sea shooter combo.

214277.overview:
A platformer by J. R. Evans released as a demo game on the 2nd coverdisk of Amiga Power #14 (June 1992). Mister can do some things that Missis cannot and visa versa, get the teddy bear to swap places. Work together to geefle for your gonk, when necessary. Turn on all the light bulbs, avoid fire and other dangers. This is a somewhat punishingly difficult platform experience, but because of that it can be extremely satisfying to overcome.

The full game was released as shareware.

214278.overview: A solitaire card game created by Michael Sinz and released as freeware in 1985. The game was written in ABasic.

214280.overview: Drive by both day and night in this overhead avoid'em style, single player racing game. Stay on the road and avoid a collision and you can race forever, but that can be tough as the scenery flies by. This game was created by David Taylor and released in 1993.

214281.overview: An Italian Language sports football\soccer management game by Fashion Design that helps you recreate your fantasy Mondial 90 competition. It was released in Italy in 1990.

214282.overview: A four player fruit\slot machine gambling game created by John Ingham of Transvamp and released in the F1 Licenceware CD-Rom Volume One F1-001 To F1-100 compilation. It is a five reel slot with multiple betting lines, nudge and all the options you could find in a pub game of the time.

214283.overview: A German language, public domain recreation of the Monopoly board game and released in 1992. Part of the Spielesammlung II compilation.

214284.overview: Monopoli Extended is a board game, developed and published by Logistic Dreams, which was released in Europe in 1998. The full version of Monopoli Extended AGA was sold as a flatpack in a plastic bag.

214285.overview: A public domain rendition of the Monopoly board game by Mathew Wilson, released initially in 1994, with later updates. It has lots of configurable game options so you can play the way to often do at home.

214287.overview: A reinterpretation of the Monopoly board game with property locations in England. It was created by M. Klicner and released in 1995.

214288.overview: The classic board game, international version. A homebrew\freeware game by Al Metz. It features computer opponents, save games, a realistic board and tokens optional house rules and multiple dice locations. Has British, Australian and American boards available. It was released as freeware in 1994.

214290.overview: David Addison wrote some excellent games in ABasiC, this one is quite well known for its quality and playability even on 256K machines. The David Addison games originally appeared on Fred Fish disks 15. This is one of the first Amiga Public Domain games ever: It came already out in 1985 when the Amiga was not yet available in Europe. It is really well coded but is a single player only game featuring the classic Monopoly board game. The game was so well loved that Parker Brothers went after David Addison, back when that wasn't very common.

214291.overview: Over head maze game, bash the little monsters over the head and collect the gems etc. Blood gore and monster guts, Good!

214292.overview:
Montana Solitaire is a great family card game for kids to adults.
The goal of the game is get 52 shuffled playing cards arranged in order. However, cards may only be placed in sequence and only in open slots. As the game progresses, those open slots will become closed depending on how you place your sequence. You have 3 shuffles to get to the final arrangement!

214293.overview: A Polish remake of the classic 1980's game, this one is marked 1992, but release date shows 2013 by Jerzy P. Mikuta. It is unclear if this was a commercial release in Poland or a homebrew project. Like the original, you play as a treasure hunter named Panama Joe, whose goal is to find an ancient treasure hidden by Aztec warrior deep inside catacombs. But beware, the catacombs are a large maze inhabited by monsters. Bouncing and rolling skulls, dancing spiders, disappearing and re-appearing chains and tons of fire await you. You'll have to find many keys and unlock doors in order to reach your goal. Panama Joe can jump and climb ladders, but doesn't have much to offer in terms of combat. That's why the monsters in the game should be avoided: a collision with an enemy leads to a premature death. He will also find amulets which make him invulnerable for a short time.

214294.overview:
Moonbases is a real-time strategy game set in 2075. Two rival corporations, Sigma Corporation and Omicron Incorporated, after having mined the Moon for two decades, are now fighting over mining rights. Sigma Corporation has mounted a surprise lunar attack against the unprepared Omicron Moon bases.

You play as the commander of either Sigma Corporation or Omicron Incorporated. Your role is to safeguard the company's future by taking control of the company's armed forces and guide them into battle against the enemy. You will manage resource extraction, base expansion and maintenance (5 structures available), and units construction, maintenance and deployment (8 units available).

The game offers 20 single player missions divided into 2 campaigns. Two player competitive gameplay is supported via serial cable or modem.

214295.overview: A four player space management and strategy game by Parsec, it was published in Amigo!, which was released in Europe in 1993.

214296.overview: Lead you squad max 8 members and destroy the opponents squad controlled either by computer or another player. Moonleague is a Role-Playing game, developed and published by Avesoft, which was released in Europe in 1994.

214297.overview:
Mortal Kumquat III (a.k.a. Fruit Fighter II Turbo G.T.I. XL 4x4) is a fighting game parody for the Amiga. It requires two players with joysticks. Each player controls one of two fighters: a green character named "Mo-Shi-P", and an orange character named "Ho-Ran-G". Both have their own special finishing move when they win a fight. The first player to win two rounds wins the overall game.

Pressing the joystick fire button on its own has no effect, you also need to move the joystick in a direction at the same time: towards the other player to punch, away from the other player to block, diagonally up-left or up-right to do a spinning jump, and so on.

Before you play, the game goes through several decision screens (including choosing the title of the game itself) that ultimately have no effect on gameplay at all.

Mortal Kumquat III was created exclusively for Amiga Action magazine, to be included as a coverdisk game on the July 1995 issue.

214298.overview: An advanced joystick is recommended for game play. For eight years now a devastating battle has been raging in the universe. the rebels were able to learn by chance where the center of the oppressive power is. Now all your powers have concentrated on this small planet to fight the last battle there. This faux vector shooter was created by Vector games and released to public domain in 1991.

214301.overview: A one or two player game that supports computer to computer connections to allow you to play against another nearby Amiga or to play against the computer. Hope you bought the RAM plates because you are going head to head with another well armed vehicle. Get them in your sights and put some lead into them, but crashing into walls or your opponent will decrease your shield strength. Remember you only have so many rounds to fire and only so much time to fire them in!

214302.overview: Motorway Madness is THE game to play at parties. This game is a four player racing/shoot-em-up with a decidedly viscous streak. The objective is simple: eliminate all the opposition. The methods vary: dual forward firing machine guns, long range missiles or a large brutal ram strapped to the front of your car. However, remember that every car you eliminate this round will be out to get you in the next!

214303.overview:
Mouth-Man is another good Pacman-clone, Written by Matthew J Barker in November 1991, This one has a variety of different levels, and the usual sounds you would expect, The Eating-Dots Sounds, The Eating Ghost Sounds, and Power Pellet Pickup Sounds, which are well done and feel nice and polished. There are Extra Bonuses, such as Ghost Peeler which Skins the Ghosts, Extra Power Pill, Ghost Repellent, Invincibility, Extra Live and even Goto Next Level which is rare. This allows 2 players gameplay as well, But not at the same time, unlike the Pacman (Kari) version which I recently reviewed, There are the normal standard Tunnels on this game, making you catapult to the opposite side of the level map, hopefully avoiding the Ghosts

When you first start, The first level plays slower than the others, I guess this was to slowly introduce you into the game, and the speed restriction appears to be lifted from Level 2 onwards. There are the usual 4 Ghosts, Pink is the fastest, Red always tends to follow you closely, so be aware of him, Cyan does not want to come near you much, and Orange who is really slow, and practically an easy pushover. There are 12 levels included, well it was released as Shareware after all, and there is a Maze Editor,

214304.overview: Another by the puzzle-king, Harald Müller (Mueller). In this one or two player game, released commercially in Germany in 1992, you have a series of magnets, some have the magnet on one side, some the other and some on both sides. You must link them up to match the picture shown at the start of the level. You must move the parts around knowing that parts, once moving in a direction will continue until they hit something or meet a directional arrow that will reroute them. There are death heads to avoid and teleporters to use to make it all very complicated. Don't forget the time limit!

214305.overview: Drag diamonds with the same color together to form a cluster which then disappears. Like other Harald Müller games like Roundabout and Soko, Moving uses the title theme of Double Dragon 2 as background music. The hand image of the cursor was ripped from Space Crusade.

214306.overview: In Movix you must move in stones from the border of a game board. If less than 4 stones ordered in a vertical or horizontal row it will erased and you earn points. Also a computer opponent included, but with a low AI. Movix based on the game Matrix by Synergy Software

214307.overview: Made in 1992 by Paradise 92 of Betsoft Computing, in this platformer Mr. Brick is the hero of the game. You need to avoid water, spikes and fire and collect all the coins on each level to get to the new one.

214308.overview: Mr. Brownstone is a well done BoulderDash clone. It is a bit more polished than your average freeware Amiga game and takes a fair while to complete. There is a card-code system that can be used to start at higher levels that you have completed. Grab the diamonds, avoid falling boulders, Make your way to the exits when the diamonds are gone. Watch out for baddies.

214309.overview: A cross between Mr. Do and Boulderdash. There are nine levels of play after which it gets faster and loops the levels. Mr Dig is a conversion of the Atari 8-bit game Mr. Do! As Mr Dig you have to collect all the cherries in each level. If you collect a group of six at a time you will get bonus points. Collecting crystals gives you 1000 points. Now and then letters will appear in the level, if you collect the word BONUS you will get an extra life and a smart bomb (smart bombs will kill all monsters in the level when used). Monsters roam the levels and they kill you on contact. You can kill the monsters by dropping apples on them. If you don't finish the level fast enough the monsters will become bored and mutate. At the start of the game you have three lives and two smart bombs.

214311.overview: Mr. Munk in Fluidland was created to celibate the release of Fluid-Pack No. 100. in 1990, so you know the music will be good. In it you must collect all the Ankh symbols and avoid the bouncing balls and evil torns\spikes.

214312.overview: The classic game of Poker and the revisited version by Axel, with the fine touch of the AxelSoftware Art Department. The game was originally started in 1992, updated in 1998 with later revisions and additional updates in 2020. A single player game with different poker variations such as Classic, Slot, Axele' and Hi/Low.

214313.overview: Bounce around and collect up the items before you lose all your bounce. Created by Jipsoft and released in 1997.

214314.overview: A variation on a space invaders type game whee you first have to avoid the invaders shots to gather stars until you become a first class pilot and possibly get some extra shots. Then, being an eligible pilot, you begin the actual fight against the invaders. Amiga Power #10 (coverdisk 10), Feb 1992.  CU Amiga (coverdisk 41), Sept 1992. This simple SPACE INVADERS clone features a slight variation on the theme where the jelly-legged pilot is able to collect increasingly advanced power-ups as the game progresses, ultimately resulting in the ability to wipe out whole waves of invaders in one fell swoop. Nonetheless, despite its unoriginal paradigm, MR WOBBLY LEG demonstrated enough talent in pure assembler programming that coder Mike Diskett was adjudged the winner of Amiga Power's 'Win A Job At Bullfrog!' competition by Peter Molyneux, and would go on to convert titles such as SYNDICATE and THEME PARK to the Amiga before launching his own now-defunct development team Mucky Foot Productions.

214315.overview: Avoid the dangers and find 40 diamonds in this multi screen platformer starring a green blob of you know what. The 40 gems are strewn around the maze. The game was created by Andrew Campbell aka Dragontooth in 1994.

214316.overview: A German pub style gambling game from Harald Müller (Mueller) and published in 1993.

214317.overview: It comes to life! Guide our hero in to the Tomb of the Mummy in this creation to celebrate organizing the Cheltonian Geekfest by M. J. Nurney. Game created using backbone. Avoid monsters and traps, gather the keys and the ancient writings and other artifacts and make your way to the door to the next level. Pressure plates release items.

214318.overview: A Pengo clone with 21 levels created by Anthony Vaughan Rartram and released in 1994.

214319.overview: Mysi Steska or Mouse's mow is a Czech minesweeper clone for the Amiga. Find all the areas without mice! A game created by PK and released in 1995.

214379.overview: A compilation of 47 games from 1993, created by Future Software.

214789.overview: Master Mind by Dan Saedén, Marty Party and Rodrigo Pérez of Reverse Logic Software is a simple clone of the classic board game with the same name. A color code is hidden at the top. You have 10 tries to figure it out by trying different color combinations. Black and white pins tell you if how many correct colors you have - white means that a pin is in the right place, black that the selection does include that color pin, but in a different place. By using logic you can crack the code!

214882.overview: Magic Way is an Action game, developed and published by Schatztruhe, which was released in Europe in 1992. It was published in Schatztruhe #1231.  Magicway is a fantastic jump&run game that takes place in a fairytale landscape. Colorful animations, superbly animated game scenes and enchanting music complete this fun game. Your task is to control the magician and discover worlds that no human has seen before.

214884.overview: You need to collect all the gold jewels in the room and open the door to the next one. During that you need to avoid the ghosts that drain you energy level. The game was written in AMOS. A simple one-screen puzzler with quite nice graphics, music and sound. Ranked 5th at RetroKomp 2018 game dev contest.

215048.overview: A pinball game created by Andreas Turowski of Mac Soft, who did the coding, music and graphics. The game was released in Europe in 1992.

215064.overview:
A 3 in one of games from Miguel Ángel Jiménez Santana of M. A Soft. MA Soft, with this game, offers us a compilation of 3 small intelligence games.  After loading it we can choose between
 1.Japanese Othello
 2. Towers of Hanoi
 3.Ston Ball 
 
Japanese Othello
 Entertaining board game in which we must catch the opponent's chips.  You do this by surrounding an enemy token (or row of tokens) between two of your own, at which point the enemy token becomes your side.  Whoever has the most pieces on the board at the end of the game wins.
 The game is controlled by keyboard instead of mouse (as usual in board games). 


 Towers of Hanoi
 Famous pastime in which you find a stepped pyramid and three axes where it can be placed.  The goal is to move the pyramid from one axis to another.  Surely you have seen this little game on a mobile phone.
 The graphics are weak and somewhat bland but they pass, and as for the sound, a cheerful music accompanies the game.
 As I have already said, it is not a game but a hobby, but it is entertaining if you get into it.  The control is by mouse, and therefore very comfortable.

 Stone Ball
 And we come to the best part... Stone Ball is a fun puzzle game in which you have to clear a path for some rocks so that they reach the bottom of the screen.  For this we have 2 little men who will push sections of walls with holes inside.  The idea is to move the walls so that the stones fall through the gaps until they reach the bottom of the screen.  When the stones reach the bottom you go to the next level, being more and more difficult, of course.

215087.overview:
Mistrz Polski '96 is a football management game. The game allows the player to select one team from four Polish leagues. The game consists of 3 difficulty levels. The game covers national backyard only. The player as a manager decides on sponsors and ticket prize, footballers transfers, stadium facilities, composition of the team, planning tactics for each match and intensity of training. During the match all the interesting situations are presented in the form of video animation. The match commentary is limited to introducing the names of players receiving yellow or red cards and scoring a goal. The club's finances consist of revenues from tickets, transfers, advertising and expenditure on salaries, taxes, credit rates. An interesting feature is the opportunity to talk with the player.

The game features historical information and team editor, allowing to change players or club name and colors of outfit.

215090.overview:
The preview of this game by Robert Szacki aka Hexmage960 was presented at  RetroKomp 2018 , it finished 7th. Sokoban remake. This game received several graphical overhauls for the 2021 full release.

Among the improvements:
– New graphics
– In each setting there will be different animations.
– The hero will be fully animated.
– Blocks will move smoothly, not abruptly like before.

215091.overview:
Formerly, in the world of Sortilia, there was a Stone of Power, entrusted to the Supreme Mage. But one day a demonic being called Xanthior took hold of this stone of power. This stone gives its owner much heightened magical powers, which Xanthior used to his advantage. Sortilia quickly sank into terror... Horedes of monsters, each more terrifying than the next, devastated the whole country. The mage was imprisoned by Xanthior in the dungeons of his terrifying fortress. 
 
The only way to defeat this evil being was to destroy it and the Power Stone. Only the mage knew how to defeat him. It was therefore necessary to free him and annihilate Xanthior.

215145.overview:
Mayhem 2 is a multiplayer (2 - 4) flight shooter with a really simple objective - destroy your opponents before they destroy you. It was created by  Albatron and Ensigna and released in 1991. Considered a hidden PD gem this game has been ported to the Raspberri PI and Windows platforms. Destroy your opponents by shooting them, you win when all other players have run out of lives.
Your ship has limited fuel which will run down when you boost, if you run out you will be unable to control your ship, to refuel, land on any flat surface.

You can protect yourself from attack using your shields which will stop all bullets, be careful though your shields run down quickly and you won't be able to boost while your shields are on.
Powerups are dropped (sometimes) when a player is destroyed (by either crashing or being shot) and when collected will give you a temporary boost.

215154.overview: Money-Player Professional is a gambling\casino game that is the precursor to Money-Player Deluxe created by Lance Haffner Games and published by Kunert Soft in 1990.

215227.overview: A Snake\Worm game where you get longer every time you eat and have to avoid eating your own tail. The music is well above average and is by Theron.  Released in the notorious Bamiga Sector One Pack 1, amongst others.

215235.overview: A simulation of the Parker Brother's board game MONOPOLY. Binary only, source available from author, Ed Musgrove who released it in 1989. Released in Fish Disk 251 and with source in Fred Fish Disk 591.

215262.overview:
The Mayor of the city is tired of the "heat" atmosphere that is spreading through the city. Citizens complain about knicker fights in the streets. The concentrations of these bands are leading to it being very Hard to walk down the street or have something on a terrace, it's all Threatened by these individuals, even the fair has become a lonely place out of fear.

Fortunately you have been tasked with cleaning the streets of all the members of this band outside the law.

215325.overview: Mortal Weapon is a side-scrolling science fiction shooter. The action takes place in 2016 during the war with alien creatures. Controlling a titanium spaceship the player has to defeat successive waves of of enemy attacks. The vessel may be equipped with a total of six weapons, depending on the number of gathered discs: Gun (horizontal fire), Side (side rockets), Rocket (rocket fired at an angle of 45 degrees), Missile (powerful missile, but fired a low frequency), Laser and Plasma. The game is divided into a few stages with different landscape and enemies.

215326.overview:
Megaball v3.0 is an Arkanoid variant with 50 levels, plus a level designer in the registered version, which inspired the DX-Ball series. It is the Sequel to Megaball v1 and Megaball v2 and the precursor to Megaball v4. The basic gameplay involves using a paddle to hit an arrangement of blocks, with the aim being to remove them all. There is an area above the blocks - getting the ball into this can cause a shot to remove lots of balls quickly.

Like any Arkanoid-style game, there are power-ups, which are released by hitting particular blocks, and must be caught using the paddle. They include a bigger paddle, laser guns mounted onto each side of the paddle (making it quicker to remove the blocks) and a level-skip, but watch out for the 'kill player' icon. Not all bricks clear with one hit, and some remain on the screen but in a different colour to show that they've been hit. 
 
MEGABALL V3.0 was the first release of the game to feature support for AGA machines, as well as higher resolution/overscan screenmodes exceeding low-res PAL/NTSC.  Reportedly, MEGABALL V3.1 was an exclusive release for new registered users only, who received 2 disks including the game disk (AGA + OCS/ECS releases of MEGABALL V3.0 with updated titlescreen) plus a music disk - that previously needed to be purchased separately for a small shareware fee - at no extra cost. 
 
TRIVIA: A fake version of MEGABALL 3 (with real coding credits removed) was released to the scene in 1994 by Hawkeye Soft, who were notoriously lame for hacking other games that year and taking credit for work that wasn't their own. Other fake versions - MegaBall v3.3 and v3.8 - were also released by hackers and can easily be identified by the dodgy spelling and grammar used in the version history logs contained in the AmigaGuide docs.

215389.overview: A Worm\Snake collect'em up game from Marco Caricati and Luciano Doglioli released as freeware in 1993. The game comes with a level editor.

215390.overview:
This game is a master-mind-clone, and i think, everyone knows
the rules of master-mind  ... if not, there is a short manual
in the game included. ( - press "HELP" in the main-menu ! )

215501.overview:
This is a compilation with 3 games:

Invaders II: The Day Of Reckoning
Satu
Willy In The Castle Of Dreams

215503.overview:
During the early part of this year 2016, it was the 25th Anniversary of DMA Design's ' Lemmings '. A game published by Psygnosis way back in the early 90's for the Amiga, Atari ST and PC and regarded by many as one of the greatest games ever and featured many blue, green haired Lemmings that could be blown up, ripped apart and dropped from the highest of points before they even hope to reach that exit. But it wasn't just the digging, blocking and thought worthy gameplay that made people love it so, but it had some really chippy tunes that sound great today, even remixed! Thus as a special release by Amiga Jay he has unofficially released the More! Lemmings extravaganza on the Amiga CD32.

So what is this More! Lemmings you might ask? Well as we mentioned above, Lemmings did appear on the PC but Amiga Jay has noted the Amiga didn't get much of a look in various level editors and clones, with new no levels in over 20 years!
