And so here we are on the Amiga CD32 with 120 new levels to play through, that have never been seen on the Amiga before. But that's not all, as not only has he made these levels available for the CDTV and via ADF, but AJ has made available his Lemmings - The Ports PDF book containing over 300 pages all about the different Lemmings ports absolutely free!

215677.overview: Math-a-Magician is an educational game teaching arithmetics. The game is played by simply answering the math problems that are asked by the program. By answering correctly a wizard appears and awards the player with a score. The game covers all of the four operators (addition, subtraction, multiplication and division) and both whole numbers and fractions. There are four different difficulty levels to choose from (from beginner to expert) and the number of questions to be asked can also be set. Questions are timed by default but this can be turned off. When all questions have been asked the player is given a score.

217117.overview:
GREAT compilation from Microdeal! - Contains the following FOUR hard-to-find Microdeal games!:

 

• GOLDRUNNER

• THE KARATE KID PART II

• SLAYGON 

• JUPITER PROBE

217149.overview: An educational adventure game created by Greg Abernethy and Martin Fitzgibbons of Rush Software and released in Australia in 1992.

217262.overview: My entry for the Amiga Blitz Basic Game Jam 2022. It's vertical scrolling Frogger, but you have a tongue with which to eat dragonflies. Once you've eaten enough, you can become MEGAFROG and eat cars.

217263.overview: Microtopia is a prototype of a city-builder simulation game, featuring randomly generated maps and three different species of inhabitant to provide for, Crows farm the land while industrious Beavers provide robust building materials, while the Moths fascinations with technology will help keep your advanced buildings running!

217264.overview:
At the start of the game, AI becomes sentient and powers up with a low battery.

As you explore your battery runs dryer and dryer. You really need to find a solution.

217268.overview: In a parallel world, 2 countries are fighting for control of the resources on the moon, you are a member of the USA team and your base has been attacked by forces of the Soviet Union and you try to recover your base and then advance to the enemy base , you will have to fight hard to reach the enemy base.

217468.overview:
This is a (successful) attempt by jotd to create a 1:1 port of the famous arcade game on Amiga 500 using 100% 68k assembly.

The display is 4:3 so scores, lives, bonuses are on the side rather than on top/botton. The gameplay layout is 1:1 vs

217545.overview: The hero is supposed to be a monkey (and the game was supposed to be called 'Minkey'), but since nobody except the graphic artist could recognized that the name of the game was changed and the hero now throws balls instead of bananas in this platformer from Matze1887 Retro Games, released in 2022. An Amiga game that puts you in control of a Monkey(no not a mouse), who must collect coins and other items while avoiding deadly enemies in 28 well designed levels, a lovable character, different enemy types, and as one person said, "The multidirectional scrolling and size of some of the levels is impressive".

218154.overview: This is a simple game that I created while doing the stream series Let's Make An Amiga Game.

218950.overview: Magic Balls is a timed puzzle board game. The task requires arranging balls in a uniform red mosaic in the shortest possible time and the least amount of movements. The player may select the size of the board, rotation angle of the ball (180, 90, 45, 22,5), range of mixing balls and switch off/on the clock. The player rotates the entire row of balls vertically or horizontally. It is possible to undo the last move or pause the game.

219374.overview: A minesweeper style game from Rafal Zabdyr that was released as freeware in 2001.

279280.overview: Megaball v4.0 is an Arkanoid variant with many levels, plus a level designer in the registered version, which inspired the DX-Ball series. It is the Sequel to Megaball v1 and Megaball v2 and Megaball v3.  This version has code to more fully support AGA style graphics. The basic gameplay involves using a paddle to hit an arrangement of blocks, with the aim being to remove them all. There is an area above the blocks - getting the ball into this can cause a shot to remove lots of balls quickly. Like any Arkanoid-style game, there are power-ups, which are released by hitting particular blocks, and must be caught using the paddle. They include a bigger paddle, laser guns mounted onto each side of the paddle (making it quicker to remove the blocks) and a level-skip, but watch out for the 'kill player' icon. Not all bricks clear with one hit, and some remain on the screen but in a different colour to show that they've been hit.

418311.overview:
A Jump n Run style platform game from Iron Gate with Zorro as the hero. Pick up the keys, jumping and dodging enemies. You have a pistol but it is of very limited use. The oldest of the place say that whenever injustice makes an appearance in our little town a mysterious figure appears from the shadows. A masked man who walks the roofs of the houses, always watching. There is no place he cannot go thanks to a purebred Spanish black horse. No identity and no age. He appears throughout the years and is a real nightmare for the soldiers. sent from Mexico with a thirst for gold and very few scruples. They say that he helped appease the Apaches, He defeated the English and French from the north and put the Mexicans to flight.

Now a lieutenant has come from the south with his eye on gold. An evil subject who makes life miserable for the locals. Now more than ever Californians pray for the masked man to appear and free them from this terrible fate, Well, this lieutenant is willing to do anything to get the coveted gold.

Everyone tells him: Don't stop looking at the rooftops, he looks in the shadows, for soon the most cunning and elusive knight in all of New Spain. Soon the one that everyone has called "El Zorro" will appear behind his mask

Don Diego de la Vega is a Californian recently arrived from Spain, where he studied at a military academy and spent some time in the army in Europe.
Skilled in the sword and above all in survival, he returns to his home where he hopes to spend his days calm away from the wars in which he is immersed throughout Europe. But those plans cannot be fulfilled, because an evil lieutenant has arrived in the region and is carrying out countless misdeeds protected by the authority of the uniform he wears.
Don Diego's father confesses that El Zorro has lived in his family since who settled in that hacienda from Spain many years ago, when there were only Apaches. Now you as Don Diego must pick up the baton and rid the people of California of the evil lieutenant. Run, escape from the soldiers who come to your farm, find the Zorro costume and honor it. But do not think that the lieutenant has made it easy for you, he has soldiers everywhere He searched for Zorro and has captured your fiancée, holding her in the fort.
Make your way through the rooftops, through the basements, galleons, mines and prisons. Whatever it takes to save your loved one and the people of California. Luck!!!!!

418319.overview: ModSurfer was a contribution to EAB coders contest 2018. A music based rhythm game that takes a MOD music file from your collection and translates that into a level that you can play! All PAL Amigas are supported. Larger MODs will need more chip RAM. Hard disk installation is supported.

418372.overview: A Game-n-Watch conversion to the Amiga by ZE Emulatron. The player must prevent pedestrians from falling into one of four sewers by temporarily bridging the open gaps with a manhole cover.

418380.overview: Drop the potato, rush to one side or the other to grab the red marker, avoid any obstacles hurtling by and get back to the center to catch it before it goes off-screen. As you are successful, the area in which you can drop the potato gets smaller and smaller. There are boss levels in this game, get the potato on the boss for as long as possible.

418386.overview: May and Yam is a game I created in 1993 for the Amiga 500. It was never released anywhere, and I distributed it for free at computer parties. It was a homage to the game Pang!, which I loved around that time. Obviously, I couldn't reproduce the original, and I made many simplifications, such as substituting the rope by a tennis ball (not sure why I picked a tennis ball...) I didn't have enough time or skills to make everything by myself, so I even ended up ripping some music from other games, and art from here and there. So it's a bit of a collage.

418428.overview:
A single player shooter set in the year 2495 where 4 convicts have managed to escape from their prison cells about a police vessel. They also managed to bypass the security code to gain access to a docking craft. They are escaping! All patrol ships in the vicinity are instructed to use Code 1: Shoot to Kill. The convicts managed to reach the asteroid fields where they are believed to have a hide-out. A special department of police are in charge of their capture. That means you!

Fly your ship around the convict strongholds avoiding or blasting threats and opening switches to allow access to the hidden areas where hey are hiding.

418458.overview: A one or two player, text only, strategy wargame created by Simulations Canada and released in 1989 featuring modern tactical armored combat.

418462.overview:
An updated version of the older Math Blaster! educational game. Unlike the previous version, this one's not in BASIC!

A new GUI greets users, called the "Davidson Student Desktop Interface"- this allows people to switch from one portion of the game to the next without all that nasty typing.

The math is broken down into five subjects- addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and fractions/decimals/percents. The game itself is broken into 5 activities-

Countdown- a flash-card style "game" with no scoring or timing. A problem, with answer, is shown on screen- upon command, the same problem appears sans answer, and must be answered correctly.

Ignition- problems appear, and upon a correct answer, motivational messages and animations pop up. The player has two chances to answer correctly, and receives a scoreboard at the end showing number of problems, number solved, etc. (This scoreboard appears in the next two listed activities.)

Lift-off- problems appear, with answer, but missing an internal component (like 2 * _ = 12). Three chances per problem are given to answer correctly. Once again, there are encouraging messages and animations- and a certificate of achievement may be printed out.

Orbit- three problems appear on-screen with portions of each in boxes; these boxes may contain errors and need to be changed by the player. Each correct answer earns a star, and the player can attempt to answer twice. This one also can print a certificate of achievement.

Blasternaut- the action-oriented math activity- you control a Blasternaut that must get into a rocket aimed at the correct answer to a shown problem. Bonus points are awarded if you can rescue floating Blasternauts- apparently slamming into them with the nosecone of a huge rocket constitutes help.

The math problems contained within aren't randomly generated, but are pre-written lessons (which are handily printed in the instruction manuals.) Math Blaster Plus! can be used to create new lessons, can be used in a classroom setting to track individual students' performance, and can print stored lessons as paper-based quizzes/tests for more traditional (and more boring) use.

418463.overview: New Modern Tactical Armoured Combat. The breakdown of the Warsaw Pact had given hope that Europe might continue its long period of peace. But Germany inevitably slipped into the power vacuum created by the Russian pullback. Our second MBT game provides the terrain of the North German Plain and the forces of England, Russia and German in a command oriented simulation that allows for NATO or aggressive German situations. Prebuild scenarios and a "build your own" system are provided.

418464.overview: Malta Storm is an simulation of the battle for the Mediterranean that took place between December 1941 and August 1942. It's a turn based war game that's entirely text based. Each turn is three weeks long and for each you'll have to make decisions on both strategic and operational plans. In the strategic part you set up priorities, and in the operational part you give orders to the different groups. After a turn you'll get intelligence to help you with your strategies. You can play as both axis and allies.

418523.overview: A puzzle game for one player, coded in AMOS and released by Finnish Avesoft in 1993.

418532.overview:
McGee is an educational game for young children (ages 2 to 6). The game is entirely wordless and tells its story through graphics and sound making it possible for the child to play the game without help from an adult. The idea is that the child in this way should become familiar and confident with the computer and grow a sense of discovery.

In the game the player takes control of a child protagonist called McGee and gets to explore his home. The house consists of a couple of rooms and in each room there are a few objects that can be interacted with. All interaction is done by clicking on the four different icons that appear in each room. When doing so a short animation will start and McGee will do something, for example play with a ball, take a bath or hide under the carpet. There is no specific objective to the game and the player can move around freely between the rooms and interact with things over and over again. 
 
This game is the first in a series of games including Katie's Farm and McGee At the Fun Fair.

418567.overview: A memory shape matching game released commercially by BBS de Saen in the Netherlands. Guus Hildesheim, who also did the graphics for this game, was sysop of the 'BBS de Saen', a Dutch modem-based bulletin board system (BBS). Translation of title: "Masterbrain - A MEMORY game for all ages".

418891.overview: A tux platform game with a built-in level creation editor. Horrible pollution is driving off the animals. Moles who have eaten the GMOs are colonizing climatic belts where they normally would not, driving off the people and beginning to use weapons. Control Tux to avoid the moles, grab the goodies that will help you keep going. Some levels imported from SuperTux.

419294.overview:
An unlicensed DOS conversion by Earok. Purple Tentacle, one of the crazy Dr. Fred's creations, drinks contaminated water from Dr. Fred's Sludge-o-matic. He mutates into an insane genius and grows arms, and now he's plotting to take over the world. In an effort to stop him, Dr. Fred sends three friends, Bernard, Hoagie, and Laverne back in time to yesterday, in order for them to turn off the Sludge-o-Matic and stop the sludge from spilling into the river, thus preventing the whole incident. Naturally, the cheap doctor uses a fake diamond over a real one in his time machine, which blows up sending Hoagie 200 years into the past and Laverne 200 years into the future.

Now the player must bring back Hoagie and Laverne, with the help of the time machine's ability to move objects between time periods, and then stop evil Purple from taking over the world.

Day of the Tentacle is a point-and-click adventure game and a sequel to Maniac Mansion. The player controls Bernard, and later also Hoagie and Laverne, being able to switch between them at any time. By using the commands at the bottom of the screen, the character can pick up items, use them on other things, talk to people, and more. Any of the three friends can also send his items across time to another friend.

The game takes place in the same area, but in three different eras, and thus affecting history takes a vital part in some puzzles. For instance, Hoagie can hide an item in the 18th century, and Laverne discovers it in the 23rd century - but by then, the item may have been affected by time and changed its properties.

420851.overview: A 2009 unfinished platform game by Team Hoi. 2D platform game Moon Child for Commodore's AGA (Advanced Graphic Architecture) Amiga computers (A1200, A4000, A4000T).

420896.overview: An unfinished AMOS game from Anthony Bartram and made in 1994. A multiplayer game which is similar to that of Bomberman.

420899.overview: A 2019 RedPill platform game from S0YS0Y based on the MSX2 game of the same name. Grab the gems, break blocks with your head to expose more. Avoid the arrows, traps and baddies. Made for the Capacitor Party 2019.

420902.overview: An AMOS racing game from Insanity Software in 1992. Overhead racing for one. Released in Amiga Format Subscribers Disk: Nr. 75.

420903.overview: A shareware city creation and management game from DIA Design, released in 1992. As with many shareware games there was a demo version available to all, but the full game was only available to registered users.

420946.overview: A RedPill freeware game from 2017 made by Tecniman and Fermix, this shooter is like a single screen space shooter like Space Invaders or Gorf but with more variety in aliens to blast.

421038.overview:
Story: It’s a tribute to the Metal Slug Serie from Clément CORDE.

It is a game composed of 3 Missions (each mission divided into a number of levels). The first mission is similar to the serie, then it forks and offers some refreshing gameplay (find the submarine in mission two if you can!). But first mission alone will not be easy to complete !

421191.overview: Backbone sample game of a fast moving platformer that makes use of the auto scrolling feature where the player has to keep moving to keep up with the action on the screen. This sample was created by Monolith Designs in 1999 and published as part of the Backbone shareware package. Pick up the coins, jump on the Ninja heads and avoid the shuriken they throw.

421219.overview: Written as a Backbone sample game by Monolith Designs and released with the Backbone shareware package. This game is a fairly simple but fast moving platform game. It makes use of menus to allow the player to pick which level to play as well as weapons in the game itself. The baddiess are mostly simple with the exception of the tank, which can shoot back at the player. You can choose 3 different maps, Grassy Island, Snowy Island or Desert Island.

421247.overview: A mini version of 1942 rewritten for Amiten TV AM0S Tutorial 2017 by Johnny Acevedo.

421249.overview: A Scorpion Engine based platform game from Erik Hogan aka Earok and released in 2020.

421260.overview: A two player fighting demo game created by Metal Team in 1992.

421475.overview: An Emerald Mine creation by Mr. B and tested by No One and the Blockheads in 1991. A.k.a. 'Mr. Mine 1'. This and the two sequels were a commercial release for Emerald Mine Club members.

421481.overview: A Boulder Dash style game created with the Emerald Mine Editor and first released in 1992, with updates following. Commercially released as a part of the Emerald Mine Club disk.

422049.overview: A platform game written in AMOS by Chris Banks in 1991. Like Dig Dug you can pump the baddies full of air, six levels.

422175.overview: A single player RPG style, turn-based robot battling game created by Florian and Christoph Marquardt. It has everything: robots, gardens, RPG elements, credits to gather so you can upgrade weapons and buy bombs. Extensive role-playing game that involves exploring unknown worlds, trading, finding objects and also competing against robots and aliens. Beautiful graphics and simple mouse controls add to the fun of the game. With field editor.

422181.overview: Guide the little guy to the switch whilst avoiding different objects coming for you. A shareware AMOS game from Stuart Fisher.  You star as Matchstick Man, and your aim is to collect the match at the far right of the screen, while the First Level is really easy, the levels get more complex over time, with several enemies who want to thwart your Matchstick Collection Plans. The enemies can be a match which hurtles towards you, which you must jump over, and it does turn around off-screen and proceed back towards you, so you must be pretty quick to avoid it. There are Cigarettes which move up and down, which you walk under to avoid them, and you can get Henchmen who are in the ground, but raise something into the air to stop you proceeding. Even much later you get Green Blobs which follow you around, which are slow, but certainly cause some concern when added onto levels with other objects to jump over and/or avoid.

422182.overview: Match the pictures to the sounds.  Several versions of this game exist. Marry Ampic up until version 1.7 was freeware, Marry Ampic starting around version 2.0.0.6 along with the switch from Blitz BASIC to a full C++/SDL with faster code was released under GPL2 and was at least for a time, commercial.

422186.overview: A public domain car shoot-em-up game made using the Shoot-Em-Up Construction ki by Nordlicht PD in 1993.

422202.overview: Read the Daily Empire, get the stock tips and make your trades. The player starts with an amount of cash on hand and can purchase from the six available stocks. The player can buy or sell as many stocks as they wish per turn. Each of the stocks randomly increases or decreases each turn. The game ends if the player runs out of money. You can play with up to four human or CPU players, the computer player is an absolute swine and will give you a run for your money.

422204.overview: A freeware AMOS shooter written by Niki Murkett and Jarrod Gresswell under the name TeraByte Software in 1993. A side-scrolling shoot-em-up game where you pilot a fighter plane who must take out all the baddies.

422214.overview: A Minefield clone for the Amiga by Richard Bernrose and released into the wild in 1993.

422217.overview: A text and picture based adventure game, published by Demon in 1990 by Dylan Thomas. Written using Dylan's own adventure system. (Source Adventure Probe 04/09). Seems to have been written in GFA-BASIC.

422220.overview: An AMOS based on the classic Minesweeper game created by Agony (Bjorn Tornqvist) for the Amiga and released as NoWare\Freeware in 1995.

422225.overview: Another Emerald Mine or Boulder Dash style game created with the Emerald Mine Editor and released commercially as part of the Emerald Mines club disk sets. 80 mines of play are available.

422227.overview: Missile Defence or Missile Defense is a clone of Missile Command. The player has to defend the cities from ballistic missiles that comes from the sky. To his help the player has anti-missile batteries mounted at the bottom of the screen, which are controlled by moving a crosshair across the screen. hen all the cities are destroyed, the game is over.

422228.overview: A surreal and strange adventure game created by David Hearne and released as shareware in 1993. Solve the mystery, knock on some doors, talk to Elvis about what to do next, watch your computer suddenly think it is an Atari ST for some reason. You know, the usual adventure stuff.

422229.overview: Create your own movie, organize publicity, view it on the charts, hire big name actors and actresses (from 1995) and gear up the money making movie machine!

422230.overview: A slider puzzle game. Adjust the blocks to piece together the picture. A game by Darren Isaac released as freeware in 1993.

422231.overview: A freeware AMOS game created by Unity in 1993. Take part in various events such as the 100 Metres, Weight lifting and more. Work and beat your own times!

422232.overview: In this shareware title by A. Perks, you take part as a gangster, making his way in the business world!

422234.overview: Put down the monkey chow bowl in a strategic spot and wait for the beasts to come for a snack then give them a whack! Bag them up and put them into the money box. When you have cleared all the monkeys from the level you can move on to the next level. More fun than a bag-full of monkeys!

422560.overview: Majsterek is a puzzle game allowing to create an own set or arrangement already prepared pictures from available components. Gameplay screen consists of a laying field, small picture and components field. The player's task is to arrange the picture with the least number of moves.

422579.overview: Milioner is a game based on the TV show Wheel of Fortune. The players take turns guessing letters to form a word or a saying. The game can be played with up to three human or computer players. During their turn the players can spin the wheel, guess a consonant, buy a vowel or guess the password. After each winning round the player may buy a gift prize. The game allows to chose difficulty level for kids and older players.

422648.overview: Mały Matematyk is a single screen educational program, designed for learning the basics of mathematics. The game allows to learn all basic mathematical activities, select one of three difficulty levels and number of tasks to solve. Each mistake on the highest level ends the game. First level allows to make two mistakes, and the second - one. The task of the player is to place the correct digit in the appropriate place on the board, complementing incomplete equation.

422895.overview: Goal of the game is to avoid being hit by the rockets but to shoot as many as possible yourself and at the same time not to shatter on the rocks in this single player freeware game by Anders Bjerin from 1990.

423154.overview: An AMOS based Tron Lightcycle style game from Cybris Design in 1993. The game included source code.

423391.overview: An unfinished cartoony beat-em up created by Insert Coin in 1997 where you play the titular Policeman fighting street thugs from the part to the bar.

423439.overview: A fortune teller that reads your runes for you. The needs of the many outweigh the needs of the few.

423473.overview: A freeware AMOS based slot\fruit machine with 3 reels and 3 holds available. The machine was created by Dimensions in 1995.

423546.overview: A platformer where you need to avoid the roaming monsters to gather all the points. You cannot jump or kill enemies. Released as a cover disk in 1990 in Amiga Fun (CompuTec Verlag) issue 3.

423567.overview: A German language homebrew strategy, or a complex long-term simulation game created by Frank-Reiner Renk ('P. PAULY') in 1994.

423580.overview: A game in the style of the vector graphics classic Star Wars game complete with a German language start up crawl. This space shooter is from the perspective of the cockpit with a heads-up display at the top to help you track down the enemies. Think of a cross between Elite and Battlezone and you are most of the way there.

423582.overview: Mystery Fun House is a port of the seventh entry in the original Scott Adams adventure series to the Amiga. The events of the game take place at an amusement park. The first puzzle involves figuring out how to get in past the turnstiles. Once inside, the player must solve the mystery of the place, going through a house of mirrors and so forth. Like the others in the series, the game is a text adventure with a rather basic two-word command parser. The Japanese computer versions feature graphics in addition to the text input.

423583.overview: An Amiga implementation of the popular minesweeper puzzle game, written in AmigaBasic for the workbench by Lee Hurley Productions in 2012.

423585.overview: A very spherical version of Asteroids made by Alain Le Guirec in 1994 and released to the public domain. Do get around to blasting these asteroids out of the sky or within your general radius or at least circle back to it later!

423587.overview: A public domain game released by PD-Soft and created by Frank C. Dudley in 1993, source code was included. You control paddles on the sides and top of the screen and must keep the spinning blades on the screen so that it can continue spinning and slicing bouncy numbered orbs. Considered one of the Amiga's Most Bizarre Games.

423599.overview: An early Aminet demo was released but the full flying shooter game from Stephen Birch was never released. It was intended that strategy elements with building of factories, mines, oil rigs to get raw materials to upgrade planes and weapons were to be added. The demo featured four vehicles, 2 human controlled, 2 computer controlled and season backgrounds could be picked prior to play.

423601.overview: The Yahtzee board game for four players as created by Dave King and sold in 1993 as licenseware. In the popular dice game the players take turns rolling five dice and, on each turn, can choose which dice to keep. The player can reroll the remaining dice for two more rounds, keeping the five dice they prefer before choosing their scoring category. There are 13 scoring categories, which include the sum of all ones to sixes, three of a kind, four of a kind, full house, four dice straight, five dice straight, poker dice (five of a kind) and chance (which is the sum of all dice). A game is finished when all 13 scoring categories have been used.

423612.overview: In this text adventure by Jim MacBrayne, published as licenseware in 1990, you must find the legendary toothpick of the Aztec god Quetzalcoatl. This text adventure is without graphics and the author has attached this quote to the game. "Language is a crack'd kettle upon which we beat out tunes for bears to dance to, whilst all the time we long to move the stars to pity." ~Gustave Flaubert

423620.overview: A Czech freeware AMOS game from Torture, created in 1995. The name means Dead Road. The second part of Honza Burian's text adventure trilogy.

423631.overview: Released in a three game pack with Mig 29 and Fullhouse, this role playing adventure game was created and published by James Podesta in 1990.

423655.overview: Mémorise is a memory game advertised for children aged three to eight. The goal is to memorise a board of six objects along a determined amount of time (more or less according to the difficulty level selected) and then place these objects in the correct position on a empty board. The player can select the length of the game (from 3 to 24 boards to play) and the difficulty level (between six levels).

423678.overview: A shareware shooter created in 1989 by Oliver Wagner and published both as shareware and as a coverdisk for Amiga Action #62. The game supports one or two players.

423872.overview: With a name like that you would think it was a single player game, but it supports up to 3. Use mouse to change three scales on the right of the window for every girl. You are the judge in the contest and rate them based on three criteria, face, rack and overall. Then you crown the new queen!

423904.overview: In this Polish text adventure from Deck Six in 1996, you are on a Russian submarine. There's not much space here. There are torpedoes hanging under the walls. On the left there is a link to the kiosk and on the right to the nuclear reactor room. Your opponent, Vasyl Papkov, a KGB officer, is a bit over-exposed. He looks at you with a penetrating look that doesn't bode well. This is probably what his interrogation looks like. You stand, he stands. What will you do?

423946.overview: An early demo of a Megaman X port to the Amiga by Master484 in 2016, it does not appear to be making current progress, but keep your fingers crossed. Mega Man X is a robot designed by Dr. Light to choose his own path in life. Years after he is created, Dr. Cain finds X and mimics his design to create a race of such robots called reploids. When the sigma virus infects these reploids, causing them to commit acts of evil, it is up to Mega Man X and his partner Zero (who is quite powerful, contrary to what his name implies) to stop it.

423988.overview: An implementation of Mastermind from Sönke Tesch and Dead End Projects in 1990. This may have been programmed using the Modula Interpreter\compiler\language for the Amiga.

423989.overview: Max Macke or how children can enjoy arithmetic again Idea and execution by Wolfgang Herweg. A single player math specific, homebrew game from 1990.

423990.overview:
Megablasters is a clone of Bomberman/Dynablasters coded in 1992-93 managing 2 to 6 players solo or in teams. There is no CPU player.

The game supports the joystick quadruple on a parallel port, which allows you to play with 4 per joystick and 2 per keyboard. This version released to the public also adds the possibility of playing with the 10-player parallel port adapter (8 joystick). You must kill all opposing players. With a bomb/laser/grenade blast or anything that can kill.

Game modes:
Get in Touch: classic dynablasters with bombs.
Illness Rules: with “skull” diseases.
Laser Games: only with extras and laser extensions
Bombs are not Bombs: all bomb extras (but without laser and without grenades)
Not too complicated: with all extras except grenades

424000.overview:
Who doesn't know "Mastermind"? Here is a successful freeware implementation that is significantly better than various commercial implementations!! Pondering fun for the gray cells... 
A freeware game by Alpha Software in 1989.

424284.overview: A single player war strategy, shareware game originally released in 1995 with v2 updates in 1996 by Frankenstein Software. Jack Rollan was looking to sell the rights to Frankenstein Software's assets a year later. Mongol Commander was described as an operational/tactical simulation of the campaigns of Genghis Khan and the Mongols (1206-1405).

424726.overview: A German educational game featuring expert level multiplication games created by Abris Data and published by SPAB in 1990.

425505.overview:
MeetBall is a multiplayer bat & ball game, although you can play solo too.
Honestly though, playing solo isn't fun. It's called MeetBall for a reason.

425664.overview: Quick puzzle platformer game made almost entirely within a 16 hour period on XMas Eve 2023

443907.overview: Moon Patrol 500 is a side-scrolling game for the Amiga where the player must drive a moon buggy from one station on the Moon to another, all while avoiding crashing or getting destroyed by alien ships. The vehicle is constantly moving right and the player can speed up or slow down, jump, and shoot (simultaneously firing upwards and forwards.)

448140.overview: An action Mini-game created by Tony Kingsmill (with Music by Luke Miller) and released in the 1991/1992 timeframe. User your fuel wisely, Collect up the radioactive canisters floating above the planet's surfaces to stop the pollution. Then land your craft for the scientists to carry out tests on the landscape. Not all all landscapes have canisters but you must always land.

McGee is an educational game for young children (ages 2 to 6). The game is entirely wordless and tells its story through graphics and sound making it possible for the child to play the game without help from an adult. The idea is that the child in this way should become familiar and confident with the computer and grow a sense of discovery.

In the game the player takes control of a child protagonist called McGee and gets to explore his home. The house consists of a couple of rooms and in each room there are a few objects that can be interacted with. All interaction is done by clicking on the four different icons that appear in each room. When doing so a short animation will start and McGee will do something, for example play with a ball, take a bath or hide under the carpet. There is no specific objective to the game and the player can move around freely between the rooms and interact with things over and over again.

468698.overview:
Micro Karting is a small proof-of-concept to see if a 3D-ish kart racing game can be done on Amiga AGA without cheating.

Everything is written in raw 68020 assembly and tested on real hardware. It runs surprisingly well on a totally stock, unexpanded Amiga 1200, but with Fast RAM and/or an accelerator it gets smoother and more stable (less pain for the CPU).

No engines, no system friendly code. Just chipset, fixed-point math, hand-rolled routines and a lot of guess-and-retry. The goal is not visuals, but gameplay feel: steering must stay responsive even when the machine is clearly sweating.

Chunky to planar conversion is done using c2p.library, mainly to show how good and fast this free Amiga library actually is, even in a very demanding real-time scenario.

This is not a finished game, not even close. It’s a tech demo, a playground, and a personal experiment to understand how far you can bend an Amiga before it snaps.

Code is messy in places, optimizations are still half baked, and bugs are very possible. If it breaks, that’s on purpose. Kind of.

481044.overview:
The plot of Master of Magic is to become the dominant wizard on two 'planes' of existence, the normal Earth-like one and the fantasy based plane "Myrror". You can do this by destroying your competing wizards (up to 4 computer players) or by casting the Spell of Mastery.

Game play is carried out in a 2D top down perspective. You move your armies around the board, fighting monsters to get treasure, and more importantly 'nodes'. Once you control a node you can summon a spirit to meld with the node and gain mana from it. You also must build up your cities so you can support and train your army. City management is very much like Civilization. You also must allocate your mana for use, or research. You must research to learn new spells. You can do battle with the enemy in a quasi-isometric perspective or you can have the game simulate the battles.

The game ends when your home tower is destroyed; you banish all the other wizards (by destroying their home tower) or someone casts the Spell of Mastery.
